newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-ITALY'S PERUZZI TURNS MEASLES PRANKSTER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ITALY'S PERUZZI TURNS MEASLES PRANKSTER.

text.p: Italy goalkeeper Angelo Peruzzi, whose room mate Francesco Toldo was isolated in a measles scare, turned up for a World Cup training session on Thursday with his face covered in red spots.
But any concern over his health vanished when it became clear that they were self-inflicted with a pen.

Fiorentina goalkeeper Toldo was given a room of his own and told to keep clear of other players as a precautionary measure after he informed team doctors that two of his club mates, including Argentine Gabriel Batistuta, had measles.
The scare ended when Toldo's mother confirmed that her son had already had measles and was not a risk.
"He wanted to paint my face too but I refused," said Toldo. "Angelo was the one isolated, not me. He's the dangerous one."

Italy are in training for World Cup qualifiers against Moldova in Trieste on Saturday and away against Poland on April 2. Victory at the weekend will send them top of European qualifying group two, ahead of England.
